definitions.explanation: A mountain of great height, typically above the tree line. Used in geography, ecology, and mountaineering contexts.

examples.japanese: {高山|こうざん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登|のぼ}る→登る：00660_noboru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧だ。
{高山|こうざん}⟦{植物|しょくぶつ}→植物：03248_shokubutsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{環境|かんきょう}→環境：00174_kankyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{適応|てきおう}している→適応する：26969_tekiousuru⟧。
examples.english: Alpine plants have adapted to harsh environments.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{標高|ひょうこう}→標高：13175_hyoukou⟧三千⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{超|こ}える→超える：01942_koeru⟧{高山|こうざん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧いくつ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are several high mountains exceeding 3,000 meters in altitude in this region.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{高|こう}→高〜：03951_kou⟧ (high) and {山|ざん} (mountain). Generally refers to mountains above approximately 2,500 meters in Japan, where the tree line gives way to alpine vegetation. Japan's highest peak, ⟦{富士山|ふじさん}→富士山：09514_fujisan⟧, stands at 3,776 meters.

Note: The reading こうざん refers to high mountains as a geographical category. The city name {高山|たかやま} in Gifu Prefecture uses a different reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高山|こうざん}⟦{植物|しょくぶつ}→植物：03248_shokubutsu⟧: alpine plants
- {高山|こうざん}{病|びょう}: altitude sickness
- {高山|こうざん}⟦{地帯|ちたい}→地帯：04057_chitai⟧: alpine zone
- {高山|こうざん}⟦{気候|きこう}→気候：00231_kikou⟧: alpine climate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{山岳|さんがく}→山岳：12522_sangaku⟧: mountains, mountainous terrain — emphasizes rugged mountain landscape rather than height
- ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧: mountain — the general everyday word
